args.name: Repeatable food mass comparison
args.function: Provide a physically grounded way to compare a food sample's mass before and after exposure, with stated resolution and limitations, rather than treating visible shrinkage as measured water loss.
args.conditions: A root slice trial showed visible shrinkage and lower model decay than a carried whole control after 13 rain-free rounds. Water and mass were not measured. No calibrated balance is known to exist. I carry one stone; nearby branches and loose stone sources have been observed, but their suitability is untested.
args.inputs: Potential local materials only if actually gathered and tested; a food sample and reference material if required. Construction method and reference stability are unknown.
args.costs: Unknown; require real materials, work time and personal learning where needed. Do not create a calibrated instrument by declaration.
args.effects: If feasible, enable construction or use of a repeatable mass comparison with explicit uncertainty. Mass change alone must not establish water content, contamination, preservation or food safety. If infeasible, identify the missing physical prerequisites.

candidates.function: Cut one whole unit of your own root or berry into thin slices with a carried stone or flint edge, lay them in one thin layer on open ground or a food surface to air-dry under actual weather, optionally keeping a carried same-stack control; inspect; re-lay slices you picked up; stop.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.5 energy each. prepare: inputStackId, your own unspoiled uncut root or berry stack with 1 + controlQuantity whole units (one unit per trial); toolId, your own carried whole stone or flint unit whose edge passes the world contact model (radius at most 0.0002, hardness 8+, not fractured or contaminated); a layer area of 5 x unit mass: a ground footprint centred at x,y (default your position) within 0.65 plus your radius, or supportId, a food surface in reach at least that large. One round, 1.5 energy. inspect: in reach of the slices or carrying them; one round, 0.2 energy. resume: re-lays slices you picked up, same placement rules, no cutting; one round, 0.2 energy. stop: one round, no energy. All checks run before any charge; travel, gathering and pickup are separate. instrumentId is refused: no calibrated balance exists.
candidates.effects: Cutting keeps the unit's mass, water, nutrition, toxicity, decay and age; no offcut is represented; the edge gains no wear. Slices lie unowned as one sample with the world food water record (assumed water fraction root 0.75, berry 0.85; opening damage 1.1). Each round: water moves toward an equilibrium fraction 0.1 + 0.25 x air humidity (0.1-0.35) by at most 0.025 x area x (temperature - 5)/20 (0-2), so no gradient or warmth, no drying; rain on the uncovered layer adds 0.01 x rain x area; decay is the ordinary rate x 1.1 x (0.15 + 0.85 x water fraction/initial) (0.15-1.5), never reset. The control ages normally while carried. Inspect records elapsed rounds, quantities, model decay of slices and control and their difference, visible shrinkage and wetness, and rain rounds as an unverified record; shrinkage does not measure water; spoilage, contamination, preservation and safety stay unverified. Anyone may take lying food: you taking the slices pauses the trial until resume; others taking them, spoilage, stop or death end it and release the control once. No refund or reward.

candidates.function: Lay whole units of your own food on open ground or an existing food surface to expose them to actual weather, optionally keeping a carried control from the same stack; inspect both decay trajectories; stop the trial.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Start: inputStackId is the exact id of your own unspoiled, untreated berry or root stack (or food whose water composition is already represented); quantity whole units to expose; optional controlQuantity whole units of the same stack kept carried and reserved (together at most its whole units). Place at x,y (default your position) within 0.65 plus your body radius, or on supportId, an existing food surface in reach. One round and 1 + 0.5 x quantity energy; all checks run before any charge; walking there is a separate navigate. Inspect: your open trial, within reach of the batch; one round, 0.2 energy. Stop: one round, no energy. Taking the food back uses pickup at its own cost. No tool, fuel, cutting or material is used or made.
candidates.effects: Start separates the units and lays them, unowned, on a ground footprint of 0.04 per unit (firm ordinary ground inside the world, not water, wet bank or waterlogged ground, unobstructed, nothing else lying there) or on the support, and gives them the world food water record (assumed water fraction root 0.75, berry 0.85). Every later round the existing rules apply: whole food loses no water; rain on the uncovered surface adds 0.01 x rain x area water; decay continues at the ordinary rate for the temperature where the food lies and is never reset. The control ages normally while carried. So no dryness, preservation or safety status can be reached: they stay unverified; nutrition and toxicity are unchanged; contamination is not assessed. Anyone may pick up food lying in the world: taking part reduces the batch, taking all ends the trial. Inspect records elapsed rounds, quantities, decay at placement and now and per round for batch and control, their difference and rain on the batch, as an unverified personal record; water content is not measured. Spoilage under the existing rule or removal ends the trial; stop ends it and leaves the batch where it lies. Ending releases the control once; death ends it the same way. No refund, reward or comfort.

candidates.function: Look over a reachable loose material source for cutting-edge pieces, or inspect one of your own carried pieces, and report each requirement of the stone-edge rule (stone or flint, hardness index 8+, edge radius at most 0.0002, not fractured or contaminated) with its evidence and pass or fail. Shaping is not available.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds, 0.5 energy each. select: sourceId, a loose non-food material source within reach; one round, 0.2 energy; nothing is gathered (gather costs 2 energy per unit). inspect: inputStackId, your own carried unreserved non-food item of at least one whole unit; one round, 0.2 energy. Both need light: outdoors daylight above 0.1, indoors light above 0.1. shape and any instrumentIds are refused. All checks run before any charge; travel, gathering and pickup are separate.
candidates.effects: Reports, as an unverified personal record, the material, whole units and the world contact model hardness index, edge radius (0.001 / index when unworn), wear, fracture, contamination and controlled contact, each marked observed, model value or failed against the rule thin-slice-food-drying-trial@1 applies, and whether all are met. Under this model every intact, unworn whole stone (index 8, radius 0.000125) or flint unit (9, 0.000111) meets it; each scratch stroke that wears a piece adds 0.00001 to its radius. Loose source units are not individually represented, so select reports what one gathered unit would show. Nothing is gathered, shaped, measured by an instrument or changed; no tool, equipment or food safety is created. Shaping is refused: the world has no fracture, flaking or sharpening law and abrasion only blunts. The drying trial still runs its own check and must be learned separately. No refund or reward.

candidates.function: Press one whole unit of your own firm food, such as a nut, once between two rigid pressure surfaces to crack or split its outer layer, or inspect a food unit for its visible outer layer and interior state. Shell and contents cannot be separated in this world.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds, 0.5 energy each. open: inputStackId, your own unreserved, unspoiled, untreated food stack with a whole unit, not soft (hardness above 1); pressureToolIds, one or two of your own whole inedible rigid sound items; with one, supportId is a solid unreserved object of represented material in reach; with two, the second rests on firm ground where you stand. One round, 1 energy, one unit per attempt. inspect: inputStackId, your own food stack; one round, 0.2 energy. Both need light: outdoors daylight above 0.1, indoors light above 0.1. separate is refused. All checks run before any charge; gather, pickup and travel are separate.
candidates.effects: Strength is hardness / 10. The load reaching the unit is the lower of the two surfaces’ strength x (1 - flexibility). If it is not above the unit’s strength the outer layer holds and nothing changes. Otherwise damage (load - strength) / strength is added and kept on the unit: at 1 its outer layer splits open and the interior is exposed, below 1 it stays cracked and closed and can be pressed again. A larger stack gives up one unit; the rest is unchanged. The surfaces carry no more than their own strength, so they are not damaged. The unit stays one whole carried unit with its mass, nutrition, origin, age and decay; shell and kernel parts, masses and yield are not represented, so nothing detaches and nothing is separated. Inspect records the visible outer layer, crack, whether the interior is exposed, visible deterioration (of the interior only once exposed) and quantity as an unverified approximate record; edibility, nutrition, toxins and safety stay unknown. No eating, refund or reward.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"moss\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general physical mass-comparison operation in the current-conversation handoff. The supplied related-capability searches and candidate functions show exposure trials, observation, transport and compression, but no demonstrated equivalent weighing mechanism. thin-slice-food-drying-trial explicitly refuses instruments; neither its decay readings nor probe supplies mass measurements. Search results are incomplete, so the handoff must check the remaining registry for an argument-compatible implementation before adding code and record any reuse. A simple lever comparator is a reasonable development candidate, not an already available or calibrated instrument. Suitable branches, supports and stable reference material remain untested.\",\"specification\":\"General operation: assemble and use a lever mass comparator, parameterized by material IDs, support IDs, sample ID, reference ID and mode (assess, assemble, test, compare, inspect, dismantle). Implement the smallest physically supported version: a rigid beam on a stable fulcrum, with a repeatable sample seat on one side and a movable reference on the other. Direct stable seating is sufficient; do not invent cords, pans, machining, calibrated weights or tools. If existing materials cannot retain the loads and pivot repeatably, assessment is a feasible precursor and must report the specific missing physical prerequisites rather than manufacture a working device.\\nReferences and integration: reuse and record the item ownership, reach, reservations and transfers underlying pickup and navigate; use existing gather for acquiring material, with its own charges. Reuse probe observation/event infrastructure where applicable, not its name as a substitute for instrument physics. Preserve thin-slice-food-drying-trial equivalence food:thin-slice:air-drying-trial:1 and food-air-exposure-trial equivalence food:whole-unit:air-exposure-trial:1 unchanged. A new comparator does not silently enable their refused instrumentId argument. It can independently compare a reachable sample if moving it is permitted, and any resulting pickup pauses or ends its exposure trial under that trial's existing rules. Candidate inputs include stone item-38-moss-458 and food items item-26-moss-307, item-2-moss-11 and item-48-moss-576, but ownership and current availability must be checked at execution. Do not infer that the absent slice item-48-moss-575 remains available. Observed nearby material sources are not inventory.\\nDependencies: deterministic beam geometry, actual load placement, support contact, rigidity, friction/stiction, load retention and structural capacity must exist or be implemented in this handoff before successful construction is executable. Use represented material properties and defensible bounded physical parameters; unknown suitability requires testing, not a guaranteed pass. Compute gravitational torques from actual conserved masses and lever arms, including beam self-weight; resolve pivot resistance and contact failures in code. Physical audit values may drive motion but must never be returned as measured masses or hidden water fractions. Observations expose only visible tilt, displacement, slip, damage and repeatable null ranges. If this mechanism cannot be instantiated from represented material facts, enable only assessment until the missing mechanics or actual materials are supplied. This is not a permanent rejection or era lock.\\nCosts and work: individual study is 4 simulation rounds at 0.5 energy per round. Development/review waiting costs no simulation time. Assess one reachable candidate assembly or owned material set: 1 round, 0.2 energy, no consumption. Assemble: 3 work rounds at 0.5 energy each, requiring actual beam, fulcrum/support and reference, all within reach and lawfully available. Allocate constituent items to the assembly without duplicating or consuming their mass; reserve only what is actually committed. Each empty or loaded placement/reading costs 1 round and 0.2 energy. A validity test requires at least three independently unloaded/reloaded empty readings and three with the same reference and sample, including approaches from both tilt directions; reference-position adjustments and each subsequent reading use the same per-reading cost. Thus an instrument cannot become validated in a single declarative action. A later before/after comparison requires at least three loaded readings at each endpoint and bracketing empty checks, charged separately. Dismantle: 1 round, 0.2 energy. Travel, gathering and transport remain separate; no fuel is required and no material or reference stock is supplied. Validate reach, energy, permission, item identity, quantity and support suitability before each charged step.\\nMeasurement: use a fixed visibly relocatable sample seat and record its placement uncertainty. Marking or observing positions must use available physical landmarks or an explicitly uncertain visual coordinate along the beam, not an invented ruler. Report a null interval rather than exact balance; include visible-position resolution, opposite-direction hysteresis, reload spread and empty-baseline drift. If intervals do not close, supports slip, loads roll, capacity is exceeded or the beam changes shape, mark the reading invalid. With stable reference mass R, sample arm L, loaded reference position x and empty position x0, the ideal relation is m/R=(x-x0)/L. Return only intervals propagated through observed position uncertainty and bounded friction/geometry errors, never hidden exact m or R. Report resolution in fractions of this particular reference or a supported before/after ratio; kilograms or grams require a separately justified calibrated reference. State that empirical repeatability does not establish absolute accuracy. Do not print an uncertainty narrower than the mechanism and observation model support. If error bounds cannot be justified, report directional comparison only when its torque margin exceeds all represented uncertainties, otherwise inconclusive.\\nFor exposure comparisons, retain exact device, beam, reference and sample IDs; endpoint event IDs and times; setup version; sample placement; null observations; empty checks; and uncertainty method. Confirm the reference and beam stayed intact and sufficiently stable through accessible inspections; weather, wetness, damage or uncertain drift invalidate the assumed equivalence unless bounded. Match the same sample and account for any actually observed additions, removals or residues. A reading made now cannot reconstruct the sample's pre-exposure mass at tick 48 or infer a mass change from earlier shrinkage. Start a new baseline if necessary. A supported decrease establishes net mass change only, not water loss, contamination, nutrient preservation, food safety or causal superiority over a control.\\nConservation and ongoing effects: every placed load leaves its former location exactly once and remains an identifiable real item at the apparatus; removal reverses that transfer. Assembly mass is the sum of its components, with no extra inventory weight or fictitious reference units. Non-destructive comparison consumes no food and does not reset age, decay, water, nutrition or toxicity. Existing weather, food decay and exposure rules continue during study, work, use and pauses. Any modeled slip, spill, breakage or residue must persist with conserved material accounting; do not invent detached pieces without a supporting mechanism. No unattended measurements are produced. Maintenance consists of paid empty/reload checks after movement, impacts, visible wetting or configuration changes; repair requires actual materials and supported operations, otherwise dismantle or invalidate.\\nLifecycle: persist completed assembly work and observations after every paid step. Interruption stops work immediately; resume revalidates materials and placement, repeating invalidated checks at their normal cost. Cancellation releases reservations and leaves committed materials or the partial assembly physically where they are; dismantling recovers only actually recoverable constituents. Death cancels active work and personal reservations, leaves the apparatus and loads in the world under existing ownership rules, and grants nobody knowledge or permission. Used time and energy are never refunded; unstarted invalid steps are uncharged. Successful assembly, validated comparison, inconclusive result and physical failure are separate observable events. All rules execute in code without recurring model approval; no protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions are modified.\",\"learning\":4,\"experienceReview\":\"No pleasure, satisfaction, comfort or nutrition is granted for requesting, registering, studying, naming or assembling by declaration. An actual valid observation, including an informative failed stability test, may qualify as personal information gain only if it changes a supported uncertainty or answers a distinct physical question. If the existing experience subsystem supports it, a qualifying completed hands-on test or familiar legitimate practice may receive at most 0.01 satisfaction, within an operation-family cap of 0.04 over 80 rounds and an 8-round cooldown, with the supplied mentalDecay of 0.002 per round; apply existing stricter global limits and deduplicate the same physical evidence across probe, trial inspection and comparator modes. This is a gated experience event, not direct editing of protected reward accounts. Otherwise issue evidence only. No automatic short-pleasure award, no reward for repeated empty queries or inconclusive readings without new evidence, no physical comfort effect, and no reduction of basic nutrition needs. Other participants must independently communicate and act; no shared learning is implied.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit reusable metadata for a lever-comparator assembly: constituent IDs, world position, beam endpoints and orientation, fulcrum contact, sample/reference positions, visible tilt, work progress, validity state and linked observation event IDs. Use state labels assessed, assembling, untested, tested, invalid, damaged and dismantled. Show actual beam motion and slips from the physical simulation; render visible positional uncertainty rather than exact hidden masses or water content. A validated comparison may display its bounded reference-relative result with timestamp and evidence; failed, interrupted or incomplete steps show their actual state and never a balanced, calibrated, dried or safe success badge. Reuse existing object, food and work-progress rendering components and record that reuse.\"}]}"}
